title: Two subject lines for a marketing email
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. A retailer sent one email to 5,000 customers chosen at random with subject line A and to another 5,000 with subject line B. Customers who clicked through: 410 for A, 468 for B.

Test H₀: p_A = p_B against a two-sided alternative at α = 0.05. Give the z statistic and the p-value (three decimals), and the 95 % interval for p_A − p_B (four decimals).

In the Workbench: **Two-sample test**, **Test** *Two proportions*, **Data from** *Summary statistics entered here*, group 1 = A.
hints: p̂_A = 410/5000 and p̂_B = 468/5000. The test uses the pooled p̂ = (410 + 468)/10000.
z = (p̂_A − p̂_B)/√(p̂(1 − p̂)(1/n_A + 1/n_B)); the interval uses p̂_A and p̂_B separately (item 10.5).
